lessons.scope: General engineering guidance grounded in the following bounded observations; no universal numeric preset is implied.
observed_scopes: Historical V100 November 2 and L40 November 3-4 records for the identical ByteShape target artifact. This is an audit of differing effective systems, not a new matched hardware experiment.
Historical V100 Flash cycle2 threads8-to6 and Flash/Q8_0 runtime-package comparisons; prior excluded Flash failure example omitted.

Local saved L40 campaign evidence only: Flash jobs265953/266141; Glimmer job266776. Returned manifests rechecked:35+24+69 files, zero hash mismatches. All results describe single-request serving, with Flash distributed across three GPUs.
source_limitations: Dates, CPU platforms and allocations, GPU power limits, context, batching, CUDA backend and sometimes prompt lengths differ. [Their separate contributions to a V100/L40 multiplier cannot be recovered from this evidence.] No SSH or new inference was performed for these lessons.

The MMQ comparisons also change the runtime executable/package; they are not isolated MMQ causal estimates. Flash and27B differ in architecture, artifacts, batching, context and KV. No claim that MMQ itself universally helps one model or hurts another.

Current upstream terminology was checked with the official llama.cpp server documentation; measured claims here use only local historical records: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md

Physical GPU/CPU assignments, runtime libraries, templates/token counts, context and sampler defaults matter. The one-L40 Glimmer result adapts a historical V100 four-slot profile; it does not validate four slots on L40, general256K fidelity, sustained reliability, or a V100→L40 hardware-only speedup. [The contribution of each changed control is unisolated in these campaigns.]
lessons.limitations: V100/L40 differ in CPU platforms, power, defaults and sometimes workloads. Kernel comparisons also changed runtime packages, so MMQ effects are not isolated. Exploratory records are not deployable profiles. [A portable optimum is unestablished.]

review.decision: Retained after review; rewritten as a general rule with empirical scope and limits separated.
rejected_overclaims: A historical V100 speedup predicts the same L40 speedup, or Ada architecture alone explains why the default-system multiplier changed.
Use all CPU threads, force MMQ on all Volta models, or attribute the observed regression to CPU oversubscription without profiling.

The measured multiplier is caused entirely by MTP/DFlash or the GPU generation, a binary hash uniquely identifies the loaded runtime, or free VRAM alone certifies arbitrary full-context/concurrent deployment.

lessons.scope: General engineering guidance grounded in the following bounded observations; no universal numeric preset is implied.
observed_scopes: These recorded Ollama and llama.cpp APIs and CANON selection conventions. November 4 probes have explicit zero reuse in the native response fields; the earlier Ollama compact rows preserve unknown despite more specific raw evidence.

Two Glimmer long trials per configuration in the same sequential one-GPU Slurm allocation; seeds 71430/71431 and distinct trial labels. CANON retains a lower-middle individual observation, while the report pools repeats.
source_limitations: The 0.196% decode-numerator difference is small at 512 output tokens but should be disclosed. tokens_cached describes cached state here and must not be substituted for timings.cache_n. Do not silently rewrite preserved CANON rows or replace an individual representative pair with pooled report averages.

With only two timing repeats, the descriptive spread is not a confidence interval or a significance test. Distinct trial labels and stochastic outputs can differ. [The cause of the variation and whether the long candidate is better on average remain unresolved.]
lessons.limitations: Recorded Ollama decode uses n/time; llama.cpp uses(n-1)/time. Templates also change token counts. CANON representative pairs remain individual observations. Unknown cache state cannot be promoted to confirmed cold-prefill evidence.

review.decision: Retained after review; rewritten as a general rule with empirical scope and limits separated.
rejected_overclaims: Different prompt-token counts prove different user tasks; a nonzero tokens_cached proves warm-prefix timing; or the one-token rate convention explains a multiple-fold gain.
The fastest single run, the CANON representative row, or a +4.82% pooled mean proves a stable long-prompt speedup.
